clue.text: Tucking into stegt flæsk, say, a north Scandinavian

indicators.note: the letters for 'a north' are tucked inside the word for the meal, as if eating it

parts.note: stegt flæsk (fried pork belly) is an example of a dish
N is the compass abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: Someone from northern Scandinavia sits down to a plate of crispy fried pork belly.
explanation.walkthrough: Stegt flæsk is crisp fried pork belly with parsley sauce, Denmark's national dish, so the example both clues DISH and fits the nationality.
explanation.definitionFit: A Dane is a Scandinavian, and the adjective or noun for that nationality is the answer.

clue.text: Convey an image of extremely delicate writer

indicators.note: the extremes of the word delicate are its first and last letters

parts.note: a scribe is a writer or copyist

explanation.surface: An instruction to paint a picture of a very fragile author.
explanation.definitionFit: To portray something in words is to convey an image of it, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Unfinished novel: Gong Ringer's Last Thirty Days

indicators.note: the novel is left unfinished, so its final letter goes

parts.note: a gong is British slang for a medal or honour, such as the MBE (Member of the Order of the British Empire)

indicators.note: the last letter of Ringer's name is taken

parts.note: the possessive of Ringer, whose name supplies its final letter

explanation.surface: Reads like the title of an abandoned novel about a bell-ringer's final month.
explanation.walkthrough: The rhyme 'Thirty days hath September, April, June and November' makes the definition fair.
explanation.definitionFit: The eleventh month of the year has thirty days, so the phrase is a description by example.

clue.text: Might Ernst & Young watch out at last for corruption?

indicators.note: the letters are corrupted, i.e. jumbled into a new order
takes the final letter of each of the words Young, watch and out

explanation.surface: Asks whether the accountancy firm Ernst & Young should keep an eye out for corrupt dealings.
explanation.walkthrough: Ernst & Young is a big accountancy firm; here Ernst is anagram fodder and Young only gives its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Might as a noun means power or force, the same sense as the answer.

clue.text: Worshipper vows another time

parts.note: 'I do' are the vows spoken at a wedding
later means at another time

explanation.surface: A churchgoer promises to renew vows on another occasion.
explanation.definitionFit: An idolater is one who worships idols, a kind of worshipper.

clue.text: Feeling down at heart indeed? Iron and iron right away

indicators.note: the heart of the word indeed is its central pair of letters

parts.note: to iron clothes is to press them

indicators.note: R, the usual abbreviation for right, is taken away from the metal

parts.note: the metal, taken as written before a letter is removed

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether ironing and more ironing is enough to make anyone feel low.
explanation.definitionFit: Depression is a state of low mood, of feeling down.

clue.text: Half of cellar wine turned up in store

indicators.note: only the back half of the six-letter word cellar is kept
in a down entry the word for wine is turned upwards, reading backwards

parts.note: red is wine

explanation.surface: Half the wine from the cellar ends up stored away.
explanation.definitionFit: A larder is a pantry or place where food is kept, i.e. a store.

clue.text: One's not into fancy elitist names

indicators.note: the letter for one is not part of the result, so it is removed from the fodder
fancy, as in elaborate or rearranged, signals a shuffle of the letters

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: Someone who doesn't care for snobbish people.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of ELITIST with its I (one) left out gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Titles are the names of books, films or other works.

clue.text: Live what's left out of uniform

indicators.note: the uniform letter is taken out of the word

parts.note: a residue is what's left over
U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Living on what remains after the uniform is gone.
explanation.definitionFit: To reside somewhere is to live or dwell there.

clue.text: Tough being cute?

parts.note: read as 'cut E': sever means cut, followed by the letter E, gives the clue word

explanation.surface: Asks whether being cute makes for a hard time.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer splits into SEVER + E, a cut E, and 'cut E' run together spells cute.
explanation.definitionFit: Severe means harsh or tough, as in severe conditions.

clue.text: Works and lectures about exercise

indicators.note: the word for lectures goes around the exercise letters

parts.note: to orate is to lecture or speechify
PE is physical education, i.e. exercise

explanation.surface: Someone who works and gives talks on exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that operates is one that works or functions.

clue.text: Make one think of theorem in dispute

indicators.note: of means taken from, so the answer is drawn from inside the run of words

explanation.surface: A disputed theorem brings something to mind.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition stops at 'think'; 'of' says the answer comes out of the words that follow, a stretch that itself contains 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: To remind someone is to prompt them to recall, making them think again of something.

clue.text: Was judge free to frolic in grass?

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go inside the grass word

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass

indicators.note: letters that frolic leap about into a new order

explanation.surface: A judge set free to romp in the grass.
explanation.definitionFit: Refereed means acted as referee, the judge or arbiter of a match.

clue.text: Farm on plain somehow filled with rubbish

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are filled with the rubbish word
the letters fit together in some other way, so they are rearranged

parts.note: tat is cheap rubbish

explanation.surface: A farm on flat land somehow full of junk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Farm on' looks like the definition with a link word, but 'on' belongs to the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A plantation is a large estate or farm growing a crop such as cotton or tea.

clue.text: Struggling to inspire praise when nursing a broken heart

indicators.note: the praise word holds the other letters like a nurse holding a baby

parts.note: to bless is to praise, as God

indicators.note: the heart is broken, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Struggling to find praise while caring for someone heartbroken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inspire' is used in its literal sense of breathing in; the 'a' before 'broken heart' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspire is to breathe in, so someone gasping for air is struggling to do so.

clue.text: All-important fault-finding

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means both crucial at a turning point and given to criticism or censure.

clue.text: Long time since deregulation for companies

parts.note: an age is a long time

indicators.note: the letters are freed from their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: It's been ages since firms were deregulated.
explanation.definitionFit: Agencies are businesses or firms, such as advertising or travel companies.

clue.text: Teacher said you got into art deco movement

indicators.note: the letter for you is placed inside the shuffled letters
a movement of the letters rearranges them
spoken, the word you is the letter U

parts.note: the word heard aloud

explanation.surface: A teacher tells you that you have become a fan of the Art Deco style.
explanation.walkthrough: Art Deco is a design movement, which disguises 'movement' as part of the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: An educator is a teacher or instructor.

clue.text: Helped firm to get involved in under-age representation

indicators.note: the firm letters become part of, i.e. go inside, the other letters
the letters are re-presented in a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, without the hyphen
CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A company is helped by involvement in schemes that represent young people.
explanation.definitionFit: Encouraged means supported or gave help and confidence to.

clue.text: Turned up fish starter, ate and had a smoke

indicators.note: the word up is turned round to read the other way

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the starter of fish is its first letter

parts.note: fed means ate, as in 'the animals fed'

explanation.surface: Someone shows up, has a fish starter and then lights up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned up' looks like one phrase meaning arrived; 'Turned' is the indicator and 'up' is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To puff on a pipe or cigarette is to smoke it.

clue.text: Clever being like that, you get somewhere at last

parts.note: as means like, e.g. 'as white as snow'

indicators.note: takes the final letter of each of the four words before it

explanation.surface: Being smart like that, you finally reach your goal.
explanation.definitionFit: Astute means shrewd or sharp-witted, i.e. clever.

clue.text: Killer groove in public transport

indicators.note: the groove word goes inside the transport word

parts.note: a bus is public transport
a rut is a groove, as in a road

explanation.surface: A murderer caught stuck in a rut on the bus.
explanation.definitionFit: Brutus was one of the assassins of Julius Caesar, a famous killer.

clue.text: Asparagus tip in tempura, battered against the flow

indicators.note: battered letters are knocked about into a new order, punning on tempura batter
the tip here is the final letter of Asparagus

explanation.surface: A spear of asparagus coated in tempura batter.
explanation.definitionFit: Going upstream means moving against the current of a river.

clue.text: Cultural and moral frame for new beginning

indicators.note: the moral word acts as a frame around the other letter

parts.note: an ethic is a moral principle

indicators.note: the beginning of new is its first letter

explanation.surface: Cultural and moral values framed as the start of something new.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethnic means relating to a people's shared cultural traditions.

clue.text: Source of tuna in salad

indicators.note: a salad is a mixture, so the letters are tossed together

explanation.surface: Where the tuna in a salad comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: A fountain is a spring or wellhead, the source of something such as water or knowledge.

clue.text: Crisp packet's final design showing text

indicators.note: the letters are given a new design, i.e. rearranged
the final letter of packet

parts.note: the possessive of packet, whose final letter is used

explanation.surface: The design on the back of a crisp packet shows some writing.
explanation.walkthrough: A crisp packet is a bag of potato chips in British English.
explanation.definitionFit: A script is the written text of a play or film.

clue.text: Something for Caesar from an address in Gaul

indicators.note: the answer is taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Julius Caesar receives something from a speech given in Gaul.
explanation.walkthrough: Caesar and Gaul suggest Julius Caesar, but the Caesar here is the salad.
explanation.definitionFit: Caesar salad is served with a particular sauce, so this is something for it.

clue.text: A: winner; B: in a draw; ___ ? Not so far!

definitions.text: A: winner; B: in a draw; ___ ? Not so far!

parts.words: A: winner; B: in a draw; ___ ? Not so far!
parts.note: the list of results runs A won, B drew, so the blank is the third letter paired with the one who lost; together that pair means nearer

explanation.walkthrough: A whimsical cryptic definition: the blank is filled with the third letter and the third result, which run together into a word for nearer.
explanation.definitionFit: Closer means nearer, the comparative of close, i.e. less far away.
